concepts.why: The patient presents with a hard, irregular, and poorly defined mass in the right breast, with overlying ulceration and serosanguinous discharge, which is highly suggestive of invasive breast carcinoma, as supported by BI-RADS category V classification on breast ultrasound and MRI, and chest CT demonstrating a mass suggestive of malignancy.

The patient's presentation with skin ulceration, skin breakdown, and exudation over the lesion, in addition to the underlying breast mass, is consistent with inflammatory breast cancer, a rare and aggressive subtype of breast cancer.

The patient's large and irregular breast mass, with overlying ulceration and serosanguinous discharge, and the absence of palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, is consistent with locally advanced breast cancer, which is a cancer that has grown beyond the boundaries of the breast but has not yet spread to distant organs.

The patient's presentation with a breast mass suggestive of malignancy, and normal serum breast tumor markers, may be consistent with triple-negative breast cancer, an aggressive subtype of breast cancer that lacks estrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors.
